playbooks.description: Turns a business problem into a DevRev solution blueprint covering capability selection (objects, workflows, agents, integrations), risks, alternative designs and effort estimates. Use when the user describes a process or requirement to implement, automate or improve in DevRev, in any industry and even without the word "architecture", for example "how would I build X in DevRev", "should this be an agent or a workflow", "we are a fintech and need to...", "estimate the effort". Design only, never calls the live API; once the blueprint is approved hand off to skills 1 to 9. Not for data lookups or running a single API call.
headings: How to work through a problem
2. Map the domain onto the graph (nouns first)
4. Design each layer, using the completeness checklist
6. Sequence the build and produce the plan
playbooks.name: solution-architecture

playbooks.description: Extends the DevRev data model by adding fields to tickets, accounts, issues or parts, creating custom object types, defining subtypes and custom link types, and overriding stock fields (tnt__ and ctype__ field prefixes). Use for "add a field to accounts", "create a custom object", "define a subtype", "add a link type". Not for stages or lifecycles (use 2-stage-lifecycle-customization) or for reading and writing ordinary records (use 8-devrev-api).
headings: Playbook 1 — Create a custom object type
Playbook 2 — Add tenant fields to stock objects & override stock fields
playbooks.name: object-schema-customization
when_to_use: Create a custom object type (e.g. Campaign, Asset, Contract)
Add a field to tickets, accounts, issues, or any stock object
Define or modify a subtype (e.g. bug subtype of issue)
Add a tenant field (applies org-wide to all records of a type)
Create a custom link type to relate objects
Override a stock field's display name or allowed values
Modify an object's schema or check the aggregated schema

playbooks.description: Cross-cutting rules every DevRev REST call follows, namely token types (PAT, AAT, SUT, session), cursor pagination, the API version and beta headers, rate-limit headers and 429 handling, and the standard error shape. Use when a call returns a status or header you must interpret ("why did I get a 429", "how do I paginate", "how do I opt into beta"). Not for endpoint payloads (use 8-devrev-api).
headings: References — one file per developer.devrev.ai "About" page
DON ids, headers, base URL — see `skills/devrev-start/references/global-api-rules.md`
playbooks.name: api-conventions
when_to_use: The exact `Authorization` / version / scope header value to send
The cursor field name for paginating any `.list` endpoint
The meaning of a specific HTTP status code (401 vs 403, 429, 409, 503, ...)
The meaning of a rate-limit response header (`X-Ratelimit-*`, `Retry-After`)
Rules for opting into beta APIs
The default and current public API version
The JSON shape of an error body

playbooks.description: Offline mirror of the official DevRev developer docs (developer.devrev.ai) covering every public and beta endpoint with fields, scopes and response codes, the Guides (webhooks, object customization, custom objects), the PLuG Web and mobile SDKs, snap-in framework and AirSync reference, and changelogs. Use for "what does the official doc say about X", a request-field list or beta endpoint, SDK install steps, webhook payload or signature details. Records what the docs say; live-verified notes in other skills win. Never calls the live API.
headings: When to use / when not to use
Limits of this mirror — know what is *not* here
playbooks.name: developer-docs

playbooks.description: Customizes object lifecycles with custom states and stages, stage diagrams (allowed transitions) and assigning a lifecycle to an object type or subtype (states.custom.*, stages.custom.*, stage-diagrams.*). Use for "customize ticket stages", "add a state", "define transitions", a custom object lifecycle. Not for automations that react to stage changes (use 6-workflows) or for adding fields (use 1-object-schema-customization). Custom stages and states cannot be deleted once created.
headings: Step 4 — Assign the stage diagram to a subtype or leaf type
Step 5 (optional) — Add dependent-field conditions on stages
playbooks.name: stage-lifecycle-customization
when_to_use: Customize stages for tickets or issues
Add a state or stage to an object's lifecycle
Define a stage diagram (workflow) with allowed transitions
Model a custom workflow or ticket flow
Assign a lifecycle to a subtype or custom object
Add dependent-field conditions tied to stages (e.g. require RCA when a bug reaches a specific stage)

playbooks.description: Uploads files and artifacts, attaches them to objects, migrates data by bulk record creation, and builds a complete org from scratch in dependency order (schemas, parts, links, work). Use for "load these CSVs", "import data", "attach a file", "set up a full customer org". Not for one-off record edits (use 8-devrev-api) or schema design (use 1-object-schema-customization).
headings: Playbook 2 — Build a complete org from scratch (end-to-end)
playbooks.name: data-upload-and-org-build
when_to_use: Upload a file or attach an artifact to a work item, timeline entry, or other object
Migrate data from another system (load records programmatically)
Build a fresh DevRev org from scratch (end-to-end setup)
Bulk create records (tickets, accounts, custom objects, parts)
Import data from CSV or another source
Stand up a demo or proof-of-concept environment

playbooks.description: Builds and modifies DevRev dashboards and widgets by routing to the dashboard-dev plugin and its validated pipeline (/dashboard-dev:dashboard-create, /dashboard-dev:modify-dashboard); widget JSON is never hand-written. Use for "build me a support dashboard", "add a chart", "modify my dashboard", "verify the dashboard". Not for datasets (use 5-datasets) or raw API reads (use 8-devrev-api).
headings: HARD RULE: Never bypass the pipeline for new dashboards
playbooks.name: dashboards-and-widgets

playbooks.description: Creates and manages custom datasets for analytics dashboards by routing to the dataset-builder plugin (PaaS versus Ponos, Oasis datasets, dataset schemas). Use for "create a custom dataset", "Oasis dataset", "Ponos job", "PaaS job", "BigQuery dataset". Not for building the dashboard itself (use 4-dashboards-and-widgets).
playbooks.name: datasets

playbooks.description: Authors and manages DevRev workflows and agent-callable skills through API calls (create, modify, delete, list, publish, trigger, and debug template imports). Use for "if this happens, do that" automations, "notify someone when a ticket comes in", "let the agent look up order status", "add a step to a workflow", "why will this template not import". Not for building or testing the AI agent itself (use 7-agent-building) or for stage lifecycles (use 2-stage-lifecycle-customization).
headings: Step 0: Check what's available in your session
Step 1: Figure out which mode the request needs
playbooks.name: workflows

playbooks.description: Builds, debugs, improves and tests DevRev AI agents in Agent Studio, covering prompting, retrieval strategy (FetchObjectContext, HybridSearch, NL2SQL), skills configuration, guardrails and knowledge sync. Use for "configure the agent", "add a skill to the agent", "test the agent guardrails", "why is the agent answering wrong". Not for authoring the workflow that an agent-callable skill wraps (use 6-workflows).
headings: Key Case Study: a customer support agent
playbooks.name: agent-building

playbooks.description: Reads and modifies DevRev data through the public REST API, covering work items (tickets, issues, tasks, incidents, opportunities), timelines, tags, links, accounts and users, conversations, articles, surveys, meetings, SLAs, artifacts, webhooks, schedules and views. Holds the endpoint catalog and the per-domain reference docs. Use for "call works.list", "get account details", "create a ticket via the API". Not for schema or stage customization (skills 1 and 2), workflows or agents (6 and 7) or AirSync connectors (9).

Accuracy notes (verified against the DevRev API-to-scope reference)
playbooks.name: devrev-api

playbooks.description: Plans, builds, updates and tests DevRev snap-ins and AirSync connectors by routing to the third-party devrev-qk-agents plugin (PM, Architect and Tester pipeline; manual install, never auto-enabled). Use for "build a HubSpot connector", "sync Asana into DevRev", "add pagination to the Trello connector", "generate the metadata JSON". DevRev own framework and AirSync docs are in skills/11-developer-docs. Not for dashboards (that plugin dashboard vertical is excluded; use 4-dashboards-and-widgets) or no-code AirSync setup in Settings.
headings: Official developer docs — local reference mirror
HARD RULE: Never bypass the PM → Architect → Tester pipeline
Precondition: three MCP servers (manual opt-in — NOT auto-registered)
A native alternative already exists in this repo's other marketplace
playbooks.name: snapin-development

playbooks.description: Entry point for any task in a DevRev organization. Use first when the user asks to create, find, update, delete, analyze, configure, import, automate or integrate anything in DevRev — tickets, issues, accounts, customers, parts, articles, SLAs, custom fields and objects, stages, workflows, AI agents, dashboards, datasets, snap-ins or connectors — even if they name no API. Finds the right playbook and API endpoint with `devrev-find`, then reads only those files. Not for general coding unrelated to DevRev.
playbooks.name: devrev-start
